The new rules recognize the locational shift of transportation users from the center city to outlying suburban areas. Commercial zone expansion should enhance the free flow of commerce between city and suburb. Zone expansion and the enlarged service areas of motor carriers will increase the service options of suburban shippers and place them on an equal footing with those shippers within existing The expanded formula should remove an zone limits. impediment to unfettered business judgments with respect to location decisions in urban areas. Shipper support for larger commercial zone limits has been virtually unanimous throughout this proceeding. Suburban shippers emphasized the problems they encounter due to the unavailability of prompt and dependable service due to the dearth of available service options. Not only the quantity of available carriers but also the quality of their service should improve. Increased single-line service will result in faster transit times, diminished damage and cargo loss, and fuel savings. These benefits should ultimately lead to cost reductions and lower prices to the consumer. We also note that many shippers testified that carriers operating within the existing commercial zone limits offer service of acceptable quality.

A prime objective of the scheme of economic regulation of motor carriage is to assure that shippers will be provided with a healthy system of motor carriage to which they may resort to get their goods to market. See, <u>United States v. Drum</u>, 368 U.S. 370, 374 (1961) and <u>Keller Industries</u>, Inc.-Declaratory Order, 107 M.C.C. 75, 76 (1968).
